name: Cause-and-effect / fishbone analysis
description: Map possible causes under categories, connect each branch to the outcome, and choose which links deserve evidence.

walkthroughIntro.inOneLine: Map possible causes under categories, connect each branch to the outcome, and choose which links deserve evidence.
walkthroughIntro.bestFor: A shared outcome with several plausible families of causes.
walkthroughIntro.howLong: 26 minutes for 2–6 participants; also available solo.
walkthroughIntro.origin: An independently written workflow using a widely known thinking method. Instructions and fictional examples were created for this app; no third-party endorsement is claimed.

lenses.name: Choose the branches
lenses.instruction: Propose two categories for possible causes of the effect. Give each a short label and an example of the kind of condition it covers. Categories may overlap; explain the boundary.

lenses.name: Attach causes and subcauses
lenses.instruction: Use category > possible cause > contributing condition for each branch. Explain how it could lead to the effect. Mark each link observed, inferred or unknown; do not label people as causes.

lenses.name: Test the strongest branches
lenses.instruction: Pick a consequential, plausible branch. Name evidence for and against it, a competing branch, and one observation or safe test that would distinguish them.

blocks.title: Agree the question
blocks.prompt: Define the effect in observable terms. Choose categories that fit this situation; they are organizing labels, not proof of a cause.

walkthrough.whatHappens: The group agrees the question and boundaries before contributing.
walkthrough.whyItMatters: A shared question keeps the later comparisons relevant.

blocks.title: Choose the next step
blocks.prompt: Select the first branch to investigate. Include a competing branch from another category, explain the causal links, distinguish evidence from assumptions, and state the observation that will discriminate between them.

criteria.text: The conclusion names possible causes from at least two categories and explains their links to the effect.

scoring.zero: No causal link is explained, e.g. staff are the problem.
scoring.one: One category has an explained possible cause, or several categories are named without links.
scoring.two: Possible causes from at least two categories are linked to the effect, e.g. unclear labels and rushed packing could each cause missing parts.

criteria.text: Observed conditions and untested causal claims are distinguished.

scoring.zero: An untested cause is presented as established fact.
scoring.one: Some uncertainty is acknowledged but observations and causal claims are mixed.
scoring.two: Observed conditions and hypotheses are explicitly separated, e.g. three kits lacked bolts; rushed packing is an untested explanation.

criteria.text: A prioritized check can distinguish competing explanations.

scoring.one: A check is named but its possible results cannot distinguish the explanations.
scoring.two: A prioritized check states what differing results would support competing causes, e.g. compare omissions before and after packing.

walkthrough.whatHappens: Participants propose and vote on a conclusion. Review checks the method-specific criteria; solo sessions can use the same checklist.
walkthrough.whyItMatters: A choice should explain its reasoning and limits.

blocks.title: Assign the follow-through
blocks.prompt: Choose an owner, first action, due date and observable success signal.

walkthrough.whatHappens: The group assigns one person the first action and records when and how to check it.
walkthrough.whyItMatters: An owner and a check make the conclusion actionable.

walkthrough.whatHappens: The engine saves the contributions, conclusion and commitment as reports.
walkthrough.whyItMatters: The record makes assumptions and follow-through available for review.
